messages.subject: Different variable lengths
parts:
Hi all, 

I am undergraduate student, working with with butterfly wing data.

I keep getting this error: > boxplot(antdirmp$coords~sexo, ylab ="CENTROID SIZE") #checar como trabalhar com variáveis de diferentes tamanhos
Error in model.frame.default(formula = antdirmp$coords ~ sexo) : 
  variable lengths differ (found for 'sexo')

I don't really know what to do now, since I have already tried some methods for setting the variables to length the same. Attached, I am sending my script. I am sorry, this seems to me as a rather "trivial" problem, but I am stucked in this.

Gratefully, 

Diniz F.

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Different variable lengths
parts:
Diniz,

Any geomorph function that produces coordinates in a 3D array - for example, gpagen - cannot be used in most R functions unless the data are converted to a 2D array (matrix).  This can be done with the function, two.d.array.  The help file should provide sufficient direction.

That is a technical reason why $coords does not work.  But I also notice you want to label the plot axis as centroid size.  The object $Csize is centroid size, not $coords.  If you corrected this, what you are attempting to do should work.  (You did not include data along with your script, so I am simply going by your script.) 

Best,
Mike

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Different variable lengths
parts:
Diniz,

 

I ran the lines of your script that pertained to the files you sent.  Everything ran fine for me. 

 

I suggest you reinstall geomorph and RRPP; both have been updated recently.

 

Dean

 

##  PARTS OF SCRIPT PERTAINING TO THE DATA YOU SENT

  # Library loading

library(geomorph)

 

  # Importing .tps data - 4 blocks

antdirmp <- readland.tps("antdirmp.tps", specID = "ID")

  # Making a 2D array

  # Group variables

library(readr)

 

antdirmp_F <- read_csv("antdirmp_F.csv")

View(antdirmp_F)

  # Classifying the variables

antdirmp_F <- read.csv("antdirmp_F.csv", header = T)

  # look for the column number in "row.names"

is.factor(antdirmp_F$Individuo)

is.factor(antdirmp_F$Gradiente.vertical)

is.factor(antdirmp_F$sexo)

sexo <- antdirmp_F[,8]

Gradiente.vertical <- antdirmp_F[,7]

 

# Estimating missing landmarks

antdirmp <- estimate.missing(antdirmp, method = c("TPS"))

 

  # Rotate a subset of 2D landmarks to common articulation angle

antdirmp <- fixed.angle(antdirmp, art.pt = 1,

                        angle.pts.1 = c(7,8),

                        angle.pts.2 = c(11,12),

                        rot.pts = 7,8,9)

 

# Generalized procrustes analysis

antdirmp <- gpagen(antdirmp, PrinAxes = TRUE, max.iter = TRUE, 

                   Proj = TRUE,

                   ProcD = TRUE,

                   print.progress = TRUE)

 

  # Plots

plot(antdirmp)

 

  # PCA

antdirmpPCA <- plotTangentSpace(antdirmp$coords, label = TRUE, warpgrids = TRUE)

 

 

  # Am I normal? - Shapiro-Wilk test

hist(log(antdirmp$Csize))

 

shapiro.test(antdirmp$Csize)

 

antdirmpMCOORDS <- dim(antdirmp$coords)

antdirmpMCOORDS <- two.d.array(antdirmp$coords)

 

 

boxplot(antdirmpMCOORDS~sexo, ylab ="Size") #checar como trabalhar com variáveis de diferentes tamanhos

##
